situation:
You are a high school senior who works part-time at a grocery store and has just been offered a full-time job starting after graduation. The credit union representative (judge) at MAPLEHURST FEDERAL CREDIT UNION has agreed to sit down with you and go over a monthly budget before you decide.

Your first paychecks have gone into a mobile payment account on your phone, where the balance earns nothing and is easy to spend when friends post about what they have bought. A savings account at the credit union, which is insured and regulated for solvency, would pay interest instead.

The full-time job starts with an early morning shift, and the coworker who drives you is moving away. Buying a used car this month fits what you have saved, but the loan payment and the insurance premium start next month and would leave nothing to save. Keeping the money in the credit union protects your savings, though you would have no ride to the early shift and could lose the offer.

The credit union representative (judge) wants a monthly budget, your decision about the car, and how you will keep yourself from breaking the savings plan. The credit union representative (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:

You have agreed to go over a monthly budget with a high school senior and hear whether the used car should be bought this month or the money should stay in the credit union, and what will keep the savings plan from being abandoned.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and after the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Six months from now, how will you know whether this was the right call?
